title: D0 aggregation, freeze semantics, and scale
objective: Group only proven routine low-risk successes while retaining reversible member identity, object/evidence indices, deterministic turn boundaries, and linear insertion cost.
requirements: A visible representative always exists before any member becomes D0.
Groups key by session, turn, actor, work unit, family, operation intent, and domain intent such as query, URL, server, capability, and URI rather than adjacency or time windows.
Warnings, failures, decisions, side effects, pins, and user expansion never disappear into a group.
Turn completion freezes groups; late members remain independent and cannot mutate frozen summaries.
100,000-member insertion is linear and retains stable member/evidence lookup.

acceptance.criterion: Aggregation is reversible and keeps exact member order.
Frozen summaries reject late membership and retain evidence indices.
Warnings never join routine success groups.
Warning/error boundaries freeze the prior segment and query/server intent cannot collide.
Nested MCP arguments and LSP operation/location fields contribute to canonical aggregation identity.
100,000 insertions remain under the explicit linear-time threshold.
Show-all and exact evidence remain lossless.

remaining_risks: A future formatter must declare aggregation intent and explicit low risk; fallback tools remain non-aggregating.

result.summary: Routine activity is quiet by default without deleting or misattributing any member evidence.
